He had the eye / that finds the fish where sky and water meet; / he met the tide each day; he did defy / the wave that hit the ship, the dark, the sleet. / He is at sea this dusk. I keep awake; / I keep the tea and wait, the tide my guide, / as if my faith might fetch him back; I make / the kettle hiss, the chair set by my side. / The mist is thick. The kettle keeps its hiss. / I hear the hinge; I hear the wind; I wait. / The dead ask this: that we recite the kiss, / the hand that fed me, and the hand that ate. / My father kept the sea. The sea kept him. / I keep the tea. The kettle hiss is dim.
